text_fidelity_a:
ibi - The Smart Photo Manager - Collect, Organize and Privately Share Photos & Videos from Smartphones, Cloud and Social Media Accounts - US Version IBI - THE SMART PHOTO MANAGER (US Version) makes it super easy to extract, back up, and share photos stored on my mobile devices. Instead of emailing cell phone photos that I want to share among electronic devices (an iPad Air (3rd Gen), a desktop PC, and a Samsung Galaxy cell phone), I can upload the photos to Ibi via a network connection with only a couple of clicks in the Ibi app.

No longer do I have to address an email, select and add the photos, send the email--and then reverse the process on a second device (open the email, download the photos, and save the photos to the device). All that’s necessary is to take the photos, open the Ibi app, choose “import photos”, select the photos, and hit the import button.

The photos are immediately uploaded to Ibi, and I can access them immediately on all of my other devices. There is no need to clutter up email or to consume precious storage space on my mobile devices, when all I want to do is share photos.

Ibi is extremely versatile. It allows you to sort and organize photos, and create Albums. It allows you to authorize certain people to email photos directly to Ibi. It allows you to set up different areas of Ibi for the use of individuals. It allows you to upload its contents to a PC or other even larger storage device by plugging in a USB cable (not included). It even allows you to stream your videos to a television set (using Chromecast or Roku apps).

Ibi is easy to set up, using Bluetooth. My iPad and my Galaxy phone both found the powered on (plugged in) Ibi in less than 30 seconds. Once set up, Ibi communicates via your home network’s Internet access. When your Ibi app is set up, click on Help, and download the complete user manual (a PDF file). The manual is easy to understand, and will enable you to get the most out of your Ibi.

Ibi is a small drive that easily fits on a bookshelf. It uses just one power cord. I really love this Ibi storage drive. It is simplifying my life.

+++++IMPORTANT NOTE: You should NOT choose “automatic backup” in the Ibi app Settings until you understand how the app works. With automatic backup enabled, Ibi will copy all of the photos stored on EACH mobile device, and you will probably get a lot of duplicate photos. For example, if you have been sharing and storing the same photos on an iPad and a cell phone, Ibi will copy the photos from each device. Worse, if you go into Ibi and delete the duplicates, Ibi will keep automatically adding the photos back as long as the photos still exist in storage on the two different devices.

You will probably want to use “automatic backup” when you first set up your Ibi. That way all of your photos will be automatically copied to Ibi to start you off. But you should turn “automatic backup” off before you start deleting duplicate photos. You will never have a problem with duplicate photos if automatic backup is turned off.+++++
text_fidelity_b: ibi - The Smart Photo Manager - Collect, Organize and Privately Share Photos & Videos from Smartphones, Cloud and Social Media Accounts - US Version

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics Standby UPS 600VA 360W Surge Protector Battery Power Backup - 8 Outlets, Black I'm pleased with the performance and features of this UPS. While it does not have the features that my other UPS's have (such as a screen that displays battery status, load, etc.) that's a plus, since I don't often use, or need, the info on the screen. This has just a simple on/off button, a mute button, and basic LED indicators that show if it's on line power or battery power.

It comes with the battery leads detached. Before use you need to remove the battery access panel (very simple -- just two screws) and connect the battery (also a very simple process).

I use it to for my router and cable modem so I can maintain Internet access and wifi during a power outage. I've simulated a power outage and both the modem and router didn't skip a beat. While this has a smaller capacity than the UPS's I use for my PCs, the 1000VA 550W specs are more than adequate to maintain a long run time given the light load.

One quibble -- and I have the same one with most UPS systems -- is that the outlets are too closely spaced, making it difficult to use all of them when plugging in devices that have a wall wart at the end. I would also have liked to see the outlets be color coded so you can more easily tell the difference between the bank of outlets that are surge protected only, and the bank that is surge/battery protected.

Those quibbles aside, it's been a good performer that provides all the features needed at a decent price.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Standby UPS 600VA 360W Surge Protector Battery Power Backup - 8 Outlets, Black

text_fidelity_a:
TV Antenna - 1byone Amplified 50 Mile HDTV Digital Antenna Powerful Amplifier Signal Booster for All TV 4K UHF VHF 1080P Local Channels with 20ft Coaxial Cable This is a review of the 50 mile OUS00-0562 model. To summarize: It works. But it's no better than my cheap [[ASIN:B000HKGK8Y RCA Indoor FM and HDTV Antenna]] antenna that I was trying to replace, yet costing several times more.

With my cheap RCA "rabbit ears" antenna I was getting 18 channels, being 8 miles away from the transmitter. According to my digital-to-analog converter most TV signals were in the range of 75% to 30%. I was looking for a better antenna to improve the signal quality, so when I saw that the OUS00-0562 model was on sale I bought it. I didn't believe the 50 mile claim of this antenna since most antennas with this claim are large, more expensive and rather directional. But I figured that even if it was half that it had to be better than my RCA one. Whatever this antenna was directional of not was not specified, I assumed that it was not.

The OUS00-0562 model comes with an antenna with a 20 foot non-removable cord. This was disappointing, but I should have realized this when looking at the product pictures. Having so much cable slack is a waste when it sits 3 feet from the TV. Before I installed the 1byone antenna I took note of signal strength of each channel of my RCA antenna. The OUS00-0562 package also comes with an amplifier, which I connected to my RCA antenna as a test - and was disappointed. Only 3 channels were 10% higher, and that was within margin of error. The OUS00-0562 disappointed me soon after, as there was no change in signal strength on any channel over the RCA antenna (except that it gave me two more channels at 40% signal).

The short version:

RCA "rabbit ears" - 18 channels, 75%-30% (+/- 5%)
RCA "rabbit ears" with 1byone amplifier - 18 channels, 70%-30% (+/- 5%)
1byone OUS00-0562 with 1byone amplifier - 20 channels, 70%-30% (+/- 5%)

I tried to reposition the OUS00-0562 antenna to see if there was a directional issue, if I was out of the "sweat spot." I did notice 5-10% dips here and there but no marked improvements. I didn't spend much time on this and since it wasn't shipped with a stand. You can buy one, but I didn't want to spend any more money on it since to me it was overpriced as is. I promptly returned it.

I will give this antenna one point though. It's better looking than the RCA antenna and it takes up less space. So if looks and space matter, it might be for you.
text_fidelity_b: TV Antenna - 1byone Amplified 50 Mile HDTV Digital Antenna Powerful Amplifier Signal Booster for All TV 4K UHF VHF 1080P Local Channels with 20ft Coaxial Cable

text_fidelity_a:
Ring Video Doorbell 2 with HD Video, Motion Activated Alerts, Easy Installation Another reviewer mentioned these issues, but I was impulsive and bought it anyways. They are all true.
- I spend a good deal of time adjusting the sensibility settings and using the brackets (both V and H) to reduce false positives, but they are still too many. My door is about 25-30' from the road and if a truck passes, even small cars, "motion detected". You stop giving importance for the sensor.
- I try to answer motion but it takes so long to load (I have an S8, with good wifi) and I got a connection problem way too often. If wasn't another false positive (as usually is), I would have missed the person lurking.
- The recording starts too late. when you go see the recorded video (because you were not able to answer the false positive motion), the video starts way too long after the movement started.
- regarding payments: I have a Piper camera that records up to 1,000 24s videos for free, overwriting after that. It works great. It always worked. Why Ring enforce additional payment is mind-blowing considering what is available on the market.
- I have installed with battery, that was really good because it was easy to install, but on the current pace (75% after 25 days) there is no way it will last the suggested 6 months on the website.

UPDATE: had to completely disable the motion sensor, the false positives were driving me crazy. Not paying the monthly fee. It's too many clicks to get to the screen when somebody actually pushes the button.
Avoid this product and wait for competitors to come up with something better.
UPDATE 2: Now this piece of crap will not enter live view.
text_fidelity_b: Ring Video Doorbell 2 with HD Video, Motion Activated Alerts, Easy Installation

text_fidelity_a:
Screwdriver Set for MacBook, Tri-Wing Phillips Pentalobe 5 Pentalobe T5 Pentalobe T6 Screwdrivers Repair Tool Kit for Apple MacBook Mac Retina Pro Air This tool set is almost perfect! I’ll start with a little background... I am tech savvy for the most part, and I refurbish my own electronics, as well as stuff for friends and family from time to time. My MacBook Pro was bogged down by a “feature” known as thermal throttling. When older thermal paste dries up, it fails to conduct heat as well, so performance takes a nose dive in favor of preservation.

I’m not entirely sure if Apple actually does this servicing upon request, or not, but I honestly wouldn’t think that they do. So, after figuring out what was going on with my laptop, I rolled up my sleeves, brought out the few electronics tools I had around, and proceeded to gut my MacBook. Bad idea. You ever hear that saying about not bringing a knife to a gunfight? It went about that well.

Long story short, I busted a clip off of the motherboard that would have held the keyboard ribbon cable in place, and you can’t really just replace the clip on a motherboard, you have to replace the entire board. If I had this tool set in time for that repair, I could have saved the cost of replacing the board.

That said, these arrived in time for me to do the motherboard swap, and before I did (managed to upgrade to the i7 processor from the i5, a mild boost in performance I’m sure.) I made sure to once again, remove the heat sync, and remove the old thermal paste, replacing it with fresh TG-7. My geekbench scores now come in above what is average for the i7 version of my MacBook Pro. Above average is virtually unheard of. It’s like a brand new machine.

But these tools, if you attempt to do a repair without them, you could end up costing yourself a few hundred extra dollars. Learn from my mistake!

My only negatives here are for the durability and sturdiness, because I feel like the plastic spudger thing is definitely going to break eventually at the sharp pointy side. I don’t trust the plastic much. Other than that, the kit is well worth it, and every Mac enthusiast who plans to repair their own machine should really have it.
text_fidelity_b: Screwdriver Set for MacBook, Tri-Wing Phillips Pentalobe 5 Pentalobe T5 Pentalobe T6 Screwdrivers Repair Tool Kit for Apple MacBook Mac Retina Pro Air

text_fidelity_a:
Digital Camera Auto Focus 2.7K 48MP Digital Point and Shoot Camera with 32GB Memory Card,16X Zoom, Time Lapse Vlogging Camera Digital Cameras for 8-15 Years Kids Teenagers Students Boys Girls This is a great little camera. It takes surprisingly good pictures. I guess I wasn't expecting much for a kids camera. It is pretty easy to operate. All the pictures in my review were taken on my recent visit to Colorado. As you can see, it handled a variety of shots with aplomb. The wildflowers was a closeup, the two landscapes were long shots with varying light conditions. The stained glass shot is the ceiling on the Broadmore Hotel in Colorado Springs. Everything came out clear and beautiful. I am not very steady when I hold a camera, so I was pleasantly surprised to find that most of my shots aren't fuzzy or blurred from my wobbly camera holding.

The only reason I didn't give this camera a top rating is because of the viewfinder. There isn't one, and the view screen is stationary. There is no way to rotate it or adjust it so that you can see what you are trying to shoot from any angle that you might hold it at. That made getting a good shot very challenging. The wildflower shot, for instance, was taken completely blind. I could not see the view screen at all. That would have meant crawling on the ground to see the screen. I can't get on the ground (mobility issues). I had to just gold the camera in front of the flowers and snap the picture, hoping for the best. The other issue is that, because you can't adjust the view screen, lighting conditions often make the screen unseeable, even if you are looking straight at it. The second landscape photo (the one on the right) was impossible to see what I was shooting at, even though I was looking directly at the screen. The lighting prevented me from being able to see the screen. Luckily, I got a good shot anyway, but I really don't like shooting blind.

So, overall, I recommend this camera. It is a good beginning camera. Very basic, takes good photos. It's just hard to use in some circumstances.
text_fidelity_b: Digital Camera Auto Focus 2.7K 48MP Digital Point and Shoot Camera with 32GB Memory Card,16X Zoom, Time Lapse Vlogging Camera Digital Cameras for 8-15 Years Kids Teenagers Students Boys Girls

Installation was simple with the only struggle being getting the modem registered with Cox. That's a process that I can't do on my own in my service area -- I have to call in to Cox and provide them with the model number, serial number and MAC address info. Once they managed to record it correctly, it was a simple process to swap out the old modem for the new.

I like the new design of the indicator lights. It's still bright, but not the shining beacon in the night style of older Arris modems. The heat while operating is not bad, but it's still sufficiently warm that it's best to keep the modem in the open to allow for good air circulation.

text_fidelity_a:
Netgear R7500-200NAS Nighthawk X4 Ultimate Gaming Router - AC2350 4X4 MU-MIMO Dual Band WiFi Gigabit Router (R7500v2) with Open Source Support. Compatible with Amazon Echo/Alexa I'm not a gamer, but I do have around 30 devices connected to a home network. These include WEMO switches, Amazon Echos, a smart TV, a playstation, Kindles, iPads, printers, and smartphones. The "dynamic Quality of Service" feature of this NIGHTHAWK X4 ULTIMATE GAMING ROUTER (R7500v2) seems to prioritize these devices, so that all of them are more responsive (faster connections) than they were with my previous router (a rock-solid NIGHTHAWK (R7000)).

When this NIGHTHAWK (R7500v2) is set up, it recognizes all of the "Internet of things" devices for what they are. In the "attached devices" list, these aren't given device names (e.g., "iPad", picked up from the device itself) but have "n/a" in the name column (and you can't assign them names even if you know them by the MAC numbers). I don't know exactly how the "Quality of Service" feature performs its magic, but now when I ask an Amazon Echo to turn on a light or a fan, the Echo performs the task immediately--instead of with a delay while it searched through the router's list of connected devices for the correct one.

The PCs and other devices that use lots of bandwidth (instead of being on standby much of the time) seem to connect faster, and they test (using OOKLA) at significantly faster Internet speeds.

My R7500v2 is broadcasting signals for both bands (2.4 GHz and 5 GHz), and my compatible devices connect with the 5 GHz network whenever I ask them to. However, I don't use the 5 GHz band for anything at present (because it's easiest to have everything that uses a printer on the same band with the printers). Thus I don't know whether the router frequently drops the 5 GHz signal, as other reviewers have stated.

I've used several high-end Linksys routers, and they have performed very well. However, I find that Netgear routers lose their Internet signal far less often, and almost never require rebooting--when Netgear routers need rebooting, the issue is almost always traceable to Comcast problems.

Another reason that I prefer Netgear routers over Linksys routers is that Netgear has no limit (or a very high limit) on the number of devices that you can list by MAC number and tell the router to "allow only these devices to connect to the network". I use this feature as an extra firewall, and find that the Linksys 25-device list is inadequate for my needs.

Finally, the Netgear "Genie" app for managing the router settings is clear and easy to understand. The initial setup for this router is easy, unless you have a nonstandard home network (e.g., my router is connected with the Comcast-supplied equipment in "Bridge" mode), and/or you interrupt the setup routine before it's run through all its steps. If you do land in setup limbo, you can start over by resetting the router to the factory settings (use a paperclip to hold down the reset button for 10-30 seconds--light will blink; unplug from wall for 30 seconds; follow Quick Start instructions again from beginning).

I have been very pleased with this set and would recommend it.

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin vívoactive HR GPS Smart Watch, Regular fit - Black I really like this GPS sports watch so far. Garmin makes a huge range of sports watches. This vivoactive HR is one of their lower priced GPS watches. It doesn't have the more advanced sports training features or build quality of the more expensive Garmin Fenix and Forerunner watches. However, for this price, you do get GPS and smartwatch features in addition to basic fitness tracking.

I tried the GPS mode on a 3-hour bike ride, running my dedicated bicycle computer at the same time. Distance calculations of the 2 units were less than 1 mile different, which I think is very good for small portable units like this. Current speed was always about the same, though looking at the watch to see your speed while riding is kind of difficult, especially compared to the big display on my handlebar-mounted bike computer. You can mount the watch on your bicycle handlebar, but that would of course disable the heart rate tracking feature of the watch. The wrist-based heart rate monitor is not as accurate as a chest-strap heart rate monitor, with a slower response time that is very apparent during interval training (short bursts of high-intensity effort), but you can connect an ANT+ HR monitor to this watch to improve accuracy.

GPS mode has an advertised battery life of 16 hours, which I think is really terrific for a gadget of this size. My 3 hour bike ride burned about 20% of the battery on the vivo, so 16 hours of GPS time is plausible. Garmin also advertises 8 days of battery life with the GPS turned off, but realistically, who buys a $250 GPS watch and never turns on the GPS? Still, I expect to get in at least a couple of long bike rides or several runs before having to recharge this watch. Recharging is very quick using the USB charging cradle included with the watch. Because battery life is so good, you don't need a spare charger for your office like you might need with the Apple smartwatch.

If you have a (free) Garmin account, you can upload your daily activity to the Garmin server so you can review it on their website afterwards. This is useful for tracking your fitness progress (speed, distance, etc) over time.

The smartwatch features are pretty basic (compared to dedicated smartwatches from Apple or Google), showing phone call caller-ID and copying notifications from your smartphone (via Bluetooth) and displaying them on the watch. If you like checking your notifications quickly and don't want to pull your phone out every time it beeps, getting them on your watch is great. If I'm jogging or in a business meeting or at dinner but am expecting an important message, I can just glance at the watch and quickly ignore it if it isn't important. I have my notifications for high-priority emails, SMS, and a couple of messaging apps synced with my phone. This seems to work mostly flawlessly with my Samsung smartphone. Occasionally, the notifications will stop working but restarting my phone fixes that. I don't know if that is a problem with the phone's base software or with the Garmin app that runs on my phone. The Garmin app that runs on your smartphone lets you pick which app's notifications to show on the watch. I do not know how this works with Apple phones. There are some other smartwatch apps like weather forecasts and calendar, but I'm not sure if scrolling through these on your small watch face is really easier than pulling out your phone to view the app on the larger screen there.

If you're comparing this Garmin watch to an Apple smartwatch, yes Apple has a lot more apps, but Garmin has an 8 day battery life compared to less than 1 day for Apple. Personally, battery life is more valuable to me since there are not yet any killer apps for the Apple watch. Having a dead watch because you forgot to charge it the night before is not fun. Also, the Garmin watch has a built-in GPS, while the Apple watch does not. This means you can record a bike ride or run carrying only the watch, not your phone as well.

Garmin also has basic fitness tracking features like resting heart rate, sleep tracking, intensive exercise tracking, step counting, etc. If you're active enough to want to spend money a GPS sports watch (instead of a cheap fitness band), I don't think the step counting is going to be interesting to you. I bike or run at least 10 hours every week of the year and steps have no interest to me. Resting heart rate is an indicator of your health and fitness and I'm looking forward to tracking that. Intensive exercise tracking may also be useful if you tend to slack off during your exercise. Sleep tracking is reportedly not too accurate on this watch (it can't tell if you're really sleeping or reading a book in bed), but that isn't something that greatly interests me.

On the subjective side, this chunky plastic rectangular watch does look like a fitness tracker rather than a real watch. The much better looking Garmin Fenix looks like something you could wear to the office, but this watch maybe not. At least the vivoactive has a very comfortable wristband that should fit well on a range of wrist sizes.

Again, this is one of Garmin's cheaper GPS watches. I think the features and performance are great for this price point, but if you're involved in hard core training program, you should definitely look at the features of some of Garmin's better GPS watches.

I would have given this watch 5 stars for functionality and value for the price if it was better looking, but Garmin seems to have made it intentionally ugly in try to upsell you on their better looking and more expensive Fenix and Forerunner watches.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin vívoactive HR GPS Smart Watch, Regular fit - Black

text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link AC1200 Reliable Dual Band WiFi Router (Archer C50) Update, Aug 2016: It's been 5 months since I installed this router and it has the distinction of never needing to be rebooted yet! That's a record for me, since some of my past routers needed a reboot every week or two (or even every day or two). I continue to be impressed with the rock-solid performance of this TP-LINK. It's not fancy and lacks some high-end features, but I'll take solid, dependable performance over flash any day.

Original review:
While this router won’t satisfy the needs of those who have complex networking requirements or those who like to tinker and tweak, it offers solid performance, AC speeds and good coverage at a very reasonable price point. If you’re looking to go to AC speed but don’t want all the bells and whistles, this offers a lot for the money.

The footprint is very small compared with other routers I have, which is a nice change. The overall build quality seems very good, and the two antennae are firmly attached (another problem I’ve had with lower-end routers). It has an off switch which is handy if you need to do a reboot. It runs warm but not hot.

Setup is very straightforward if you want to keep the default settings. Basically just plug it into a PC, access the router menu with your browser, set the network name and password, and you’re done. You can access more advanced features if needed, but for a basic setup the time required is less than 5 minutes.

Performance has been impressive. I also have AC routers from D-Link and Linksys that are far more costly than this, but this little guy holds his own when it comes to coverage and throughput. For example, I get Internet connection speeds of about 62mBps with my D-Link DIR-880L. This router, with the same PC and network card, gives me 50mBps. Wireless coverage is a little more spotty with this router on fringe areas (e.g., for a PC located a floor above and at the opposite end of the house from the router) but it still maintains a connection, albeit at lower speeds.

This does lack some features that could be helpful for some situations. It has a USB port, but only has one, and it’s a 2.0 USB port. It lacks a gigabit port as well. But again, for the price, it offers a lot of performance. So far I’ve had zero problems or glitches.

This router won’t excite a power user or satisfy complex networking requirements/demands, but for the basics, it gets the job done with solid speed and performance. Well worth considering if you’re looking for an inexpensive router.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link AC1200 Reliable Dual Band WiFi Router (Archer C50)

text_fidelity_a:
Nyne Boost Waterproof Portable Bluetooth Speakers with Premium Stereo Sound - IP67 Water & Dust Proof, 20 Hours Play-time, 100 ft Range, Built-in Power Bank and Mic, Loud Wireless Speaker,Grey Having outdoor safe speakers is essential for my household. Not only do I have audiophiles who are addicted to headphones and speakers, I have a husband who insists on taking his speakers to outdoor jobs. that is fine except when the job turns out to have a sudden rainstorm or high dust going on. Before giving it to him, I had our daughter put it through the grind at work (food prep) and in town events. Let's see how this speaker performs..

WHAT IS THIS SPEAKER LIKE?
This speaker is gray in color. The housing is very rubbery in consistency. The right side of the speaker has sealed controls under a rubberized pad over top of the buttons. The speaker stays put and is heavier than expected.

ON/OFF BUTTON/PAIRING
Holding down for over a second powers up the speaker. Next to the power button is the PAIRING button. This is not for pairing the speaker to a device but it is for pairing with another speaker just like it. A coworker with my daughter has this speaker and they tested it out- works GREAT so you now get two synced speakers.

CALLS BUTTON
You can send and receive calls with this button. You can also access your voice commands on your phone with this button.

VOLUME BUTTON
This is plus or minus sound controls. You can also skip by holding down- + is forward, - is backward.

PAUSE/PLAY
You can control pausing and playing with this button.

DOCKING
USB for charging, mini USB port (to use to charge a device if need be), and auxiliary outlet for like an old MP3 player or other device that does not have Bluetooth capability.

CHARGING INDICATOR LIGHT
Red when charging and turns white when fully charged. Will indicate when the power is running low so you will know.

SOUND QUALITY
Sound quality with this is very good. My daughter has a coworker with the same speaker so they both have had a chance to experiment with their speakers. So far it has been a great speaker. The balance of the recording of course affects the speaker, but so far it has not been overly muffled, out of balance, etc. Where you put the speaker affects how it sounds too.

When put on the floor, it really does sound better than on, say top of a box, or couch, etc. A very hard surface seems to really make it sound best.

VOLUME
When using the volume controls on the speaker, the sound is better than when you use the volume controls on the device (tablet, phone, etc).

DURABILITY
This speaker was taken to a huge town chicken and biscuit dinner and was dropped and still is working perfectly.

BATTERY
Two 10 hour shifts at full volume, and this speaker kicked through it all before needing to be recharged.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a really nice durable speaker that is dustproof, shock proof, and supposedly water proof, this is a good choice. It is solid, has decent sound , and even can be synced with another speaker if you get two of these for coverage around a room.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is a decent speaker, and I feel more comfortable having my husband use this on his jobs than the other really nice speaker he was beating up.
text_fidelity_b: Nyne Boost Waterproof Portable Bluetooth Speakers with Premium Stereo Sound - IP67 Water & Dust Proof, 20 Hours Play-time, 100 ft Range, Built-in Power Bank and Mic, Loud Wireless Speaker,Grey

text_fidelity_a:
TomTom XL 350 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator The good:

Lane guidance. I like to plan my turns and exits, especially in thick traffic. I hate it when the passenger who claims to know the way suddenly says "Left turn here!" to feet from the intersection when I'm in the right lane and the middle and left lanes are packed with traffic. No more. Tom Tom says things like, "Take a right on 17th street, then a left on Maritime Road, giving me time to get into that left lane." It also gives you lane guidance for exiting the highway, when it's right two lanes for this highway, and middle two for this bridge and left one for the other bridge. You can see on screen, and it tells you aloud, which land you want.

It tells you "left turn here", which is good when the street sign is missing or obscured.

It adapts quickly. It seems to know traffic laws, so it doesn't try to put you the wrong way on a one way the way Mapquest did in the early days.

It tracks your speed.

The route chosen to a familiar location surprised me, but thinking it over, it was the most direct route. I normal go one exit on the highway. It had me go a few very small side streets instead.

It works in or out of the car, for those who want to use it for camping or geocaching.

The bad:

Even on the loudest setting, it's a little hard to hear. The pronunciation is off, which one might expect, but the volume is poor. It's hard to hear, even with no one talking in the car. Good luck if you've got kids in the back seat.

It was a little hard to figure out. It wants the street then the number, and I tried offering the full address. Once I figured it out, it was pretty easy and did a great job.
text_fidelity_b: TomTom XL 350 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator

Microsoft Surface Book 13.5" (Intel Core i5, 8GB RAM, 256 GB) So my only complaint about Microsoft devices as a whole is their lack of compatibility with Linux. This one is better than the other 4 I have owned. It still isn't working well with CentOS, but Kubuntu works awesomely, and I also have Kali running. I've got a tripple boot (with Windows as well) set up, and the whole thing took about 5 hours to set up. If you're looking for a laptop to run Linux on, that is light and has a great battery, the choice is this one or the XPS. The XPS (my friend has one) doesn't run touchscreen, but it is lighter than this one and gets even better battery...

Overall, this laptop has a great battery, a great screen, and runs Linux with very little effort. The only downsides are the requirement to have power connected in order to detach the screen (yes, the button does work in Linux), the fact that all ports (USB, SD and charging included) are on the base (so in tablet mode it can't charge, can't read an SD card, and can't use a USB device), and the fact that it is so sealed that you can't upgrade or repair it yourself. Those are the reasons I dropped one star (personally, I'd drop 4 stars for all that, but I know most people wouldn't).
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Surface Book 13.5" (Intel Core i5, 8GB RAM, 256 GB)

text_fidelity_a:
Regetek 7" Double DIN Touchscreen in Dash Bluetooth Car Stereo Mp3 Audio 1080P Video Player FM Radio/AM Radio/TF/USB/AUX-in + Remote Control I received this as a free review sample. The reason why I subtracted a star is the cables (both the one from the charger to the control module, and the 3.5mm connection) are hardwired. This means that if either cable becomes damaged it can cost more to repair than to replace, unless you have the skills to repair them. Had the charger been configured with a micro USB port and the control module with a 3.5mm port for separate cables that can be easily purchased just about anywhere (including pharmacies and supermarkets these days), a damaged cable would be an easy swap and the value and utility of this solution been a lot more.

Operationally, this kit functions as promised. The mic will pass through commands if your phone has voice recognition, and the overall quality of sound is more a function of your vehicle's stereo system than this unit. Since my vehicle is already bluetooth-enabled I used a small, powered speaker with a 3.5mm input to test this. Since the cable, as mentioned, is fixed I had to still perform the test in my vehicle. The sound quality was overall good, and making and receiving test calls were easy and the connections clear enough to be heard without 'can you hear me now?'

Surprisingly the extra USB port in the charger was relatively fast, and proved to be as good as any high-speed (but non QC) charger on both my Note 4 and a friend's iPhone 5S. In fact, that is why I only subtracted one star because while the cable issue does detract, the charging capability of the extra port is better than I expected.

Bottom line: this is an OK hand's free solution for older vehicles that have an AUX port, but no bluetooth (and you NEED an AUX port to make this work.) Since the control module is hardwired into a lighter-style charger you cannot use this with a home stereo that does not have bluetooth, but does have 3.5mm input. There are similar solutions that use basically the same design, but replaceable cables that do allow this, so this one is restricted to vehicle-only use. If that is all you need, this one does perform as claimed.
text_fidelity_b: Regetek 7" Double DIN Touchscreen in Dash Bluetooth Car Stereo Mp3 Audio 1080P Video Player FM Radio/AM Radio/TF/USB/AUX-in + Remote Control

SAMSUNG X5 Portable SSD - 2TB - Thunderbolt 3 External SSD (MU-PB2T0B/AM) Gray/Red If you have a Thunderbolt 3-equipped computer, this drive provides speeds approaching the highest-end built-in SSDs. Case in point: I have a 2018 MacBook Pro with top specs. Its internal SSD is a screamer. And, as you can see from my screen shots, the X5 is right in the same neighborhood. These tests were run on my computer while it was running a bunch of other things (Word, Excel, VMWare Fusion, Mail.app, Safari with about 15 tabs open), so it represents real-world use.

And, as you can see, the X5 is really fast. If you need speed and have Thunderbolt 3, this is a great drive.

Installation was easy. My Mac recognized the drive right away. I could've just used it, but Samsung provides a utility on the drive for enabling its onboard encryption and keeping its firmware up to data. Recommended.

(But do make sure your computer has Thunderbolt 3. You can't tell just by looking at the ports, as TB3 is implemented as a superset of USB-C. So, Thunderbolt 3 is USB-C but the converse is not true. Similarly, previous-rev Thunderbolt interfaces aren't forward-compatible to TB3 devices. Some of the one-star reviews of this drive are clearly from folks who didn't know these issues.)
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG X5 Portable SSD - 2TB - Thunderbolt 3 External SSD (MU-PB2T0B/AM) Gray/Red

text_fidelity_a:
Gator Cases 28" Creative Pro Bag for Video Camera Systems with Wheels & Pull Handle (GCPRVCAM28W) Let me start off by saying I work in freelance video and I love how much I can fit inside this case! I've been using a Pelican 1510 as my go-to travel carrier, so that's mostly what I'm comparing this to. For starters, this is a longer case so in addition to my cameras, lenses, batteries and other accessories, it has a long open sleeve that can even fit a light stand or small tripod! For extra versatility, the whole interior can actually be pulled out (it has its own handle straps if you want to use it as its own carrier), which then frees up the ample storage space inside the case as a separate giant unit (see pictures to illustrate). There are also plenty of pockets on the inside, as well as the outside and front of the case. Of course, for a case this size there is the requisite wheels and carrying handle.
The only things I like better about my Pelican case, however, are the toughness and waterproofing. This bag comes with a rain cover which you can keep inside the case, however I don't like the idea of having to carry around a cover inside the bag, then take it out and put it on if it starts raining. The Pelican cases are air tight by simply closing them, no rain cover needed. The Pelican cases also are tough enough that they can be stacked under other equipment, thrown into a corner, sat on, stood on, etc, and 99% of the time come out unscathed. That's more than I can say for this bag. I bring this bag on gigs that I'm not worried about those things happening, because I can fit what I normally take in 3 separate bags into just this one. You could get a Pelican style case in this size, however it would cost quite a bit more than the asking price of this one. I think for the price this is a great tool to keep your stuff organized and ready to go whenever you are!
text_fidelity_b: Gator Cases 28" Creative Pro Bag for Video Camera Systems with Wheels & Pull Handle (GCPRVCAM28W)

text_fidelity_a: Amazon Basics Wire Cable Management Sleeve Cover Organizer - Zipper, 40-Inch, Black, 2-Pack These sleeves really work and they are big enough to comfortably accommodate at least 4 to 6 thick cables; maybe more thin cables.  At first I thought 20 inches (the length of the sleeves) seemed a little short, but since cables start and terminate at different points, anything longer might not work as the run distance would be too long and you might have to "backtrack" on a cable after it comes out the end.  I have masses of cables running everywhere and just one of these helped make things neater.  Now I need to use the other 3 in the package.  I might even buy a second package of 4 if I still have cables that need straightening up.  The nicest feature of these sleeves is that you don't have to feed the cables through them.  They unzip for the entire length and you just lay the cables into the sleeve and zip it up.  No need to disconnect cables.  This is a genius idea and I love it.  I have tried other methods to keep cables together, such as zip ties, but they don't work nearly as well as these.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Wire Cable Management Sleeve Cover Organizer - Zipper, 40-Inch, Black, 2-Pack

XBOOM Mini Portable Capsule Speaker with Rechargeable Battery and Enhanced Bass+ Resonator (Mini - Black) -1 pack When listening to your favorite tunes, videos, etc., sound enhancement makes a noticeable difference. Cell phones and other electronic devices are often quite lacking in sound quality, mainly because the sounds are directed to a tiny speaker. An enhancement can make music and other noises come to life and the Xboom Mini Portable Capsule Speaker is ready to serve in this regard.

This speaker is small, stylish, and versatile and I have used it with several different electronic devices. It is very compact in size, operates on a rechargeable battery, and can be collapsed to a size so small that it fits into tight quarters with ease. Just plug it into a cell phone, tablet, or other device, flip the switch, adjust the volume, and listen to your favorite music like never before.

I was skeptical when I first used this device because it just didn’t seem capable of much. It looks cool, but it’s just so small. How much sound could possibly release itself from such a tiny speaker, I wondered. But a few uses demonstrate that this little speaker is capable of many great things. It doesn’t produces deafening decibels, no. But the volume is much louder than that of a typical cell phone or tablet. And the bass enhancement makes it sound like a true stereo speaker. I was pleasantly surprised when I used it and I couldn’t believe something so seemingly miniscule and insignificant would be capable of so much.

The battery in this little guy is good for about 12 hours of use, according to the manufacturer. Truth is, I have never had to worry about this because, if you use the USB cord and plug into a computer, you don’t need to charge it first. My kids like to use it in their cell phones and they are always careful to maintain the charge. Twelve hours is a long time and the reason I know it’s a long time is because, in a few months of use, it has never exhausted its charge. The kiddos can use it on a lengthy road trip and it maintains its juice.

Many smaller electronics need better sound and the Xboom Mini Portable Capsule Speaker is a very good device for improving your next audio experience. Multiple units can be plugged together for even greater satisfaction but even if you have only one, you will find this little gadget is more than able to deliver very good sound quality. It’s one of my favorite electronic enhancers and one I and my kids will continue to use.
text_fidelity_b: XBOOM Mini Portable Capsule Speaker with Rechargeable Battery and Enhanced Bass+ Resonator (Mini - Black) -1 pack

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm FinePix J40 12.2 MP Digital Camera with 3x Optical Zoom and 3-Inch LCD (Includes 2 GB SD Memory Card) The camera is $[..]for gosh sakes! It's an amazing little piece of technology. The 3X optics and 12.2MP CMOS camera are well matched in the optical train to provide a great image for casual photos adequate for most users. It's the simplest start-up I've ever seen. The viewer LCD provides a maximum size to the package. `The manual' is 7 steps of which 4 include inserting memory, battery, charging battery and turning it on. It's `point and shoot' in the extreme.

I work in the domain of optics & imaging design. My wife has a 5 year old Fuji camera of this same genre that I've gone to some lengths to compare with Nikon and Canon in this low cost market. Without getting technical ... for the old Fuji, there are no user discernable image quality differences. The Fuji optics were superior (i.e. best objective lens light capture and transfer). Take your pick between the 3 on the backend image processing system/PC interface.

My wife has carried the 5 year old Fuji in her purse every day ... that's a technically demanding reliability challenge. Fuji can be relied on to deliver the best value for money in an image capture platform if you're designing a million dollar platform or this $69 platform. You're not paying the premium for the huge advertisement budget of Nikon and Canon when you buy Fuji. I think you just get a better camera.

I can't speak to this unit's reliability for now. A 3x optical train with autofocus, f-stop, etc mechanisms and micro motors are robust to a point. They will all fail, even the highest dollar product, if exposed to the wrong environment (g-shock, sand, salt spray, thermal shock, etc).

One reviewer mentioned software loading problems. I had absolutely no problems on a Windows 7, 64bit OS.

You can't go wrong with this device. It's an excellent camera for you or the kids or the g-kids for Xmas.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm FinePix J40 12.2 MP Digital Camera with 3x Optical Zoom and 3-Inch LCD (Includes 2 GB SD Memory Card)

text_fidelity_a: Apple iPod Touch (4th Generation) Old Model I already own an iTouch 16GB 1st gen. It still works well but I needed more storage for my ever growing TV show and movie collection. I bought mine overseas at a military store that could not keep these in stock. My first thought was how thin it was compared to my old iTouch, nearly half the size. But, recent technology has packed so much more into this small case. I didn't read the specs. I already knew most of what it was supposed to do. I did not know about the external speakers, which sound fine if you make some adjustments. I've watched Blackadder's Christmas Carol and the clarity was amazing. I took some pictures and I don't really like the stills because they seem blurred. The video camera, however, is great. I downloaded the Kindle reader app and was able to sync my existing library. It's nice to see my bookcovers in color and reading the written page is clear and easy on the eyes. The iBooks app is also nice for reading PDFs. Getting online was really quick after locating the nearest free Wi-Fi signal. I use my iTouch mainly for listening to Audible audiobooks, of which I have a massive collection. Because of its size, it is truly more mobile and easier to carry than my Sony Touch ereader, and I don't need additional light to read the screen. Only my netbook gives me more entertainment options because it have much more storage and an external keyboard. The virtual keyboard is small and does the job for typing in website addresses. I would rather use the voice recorder to take notes. I do have a capacative stylus to avoid fingerprints but I will get a screen protector soon. Overall, I paid full price in case I needed to return it for problems. So far, it's been a good deal.
text_fidelity_b: Apple iPod Touch (4th Generation) Old Model

However, when I check the time in the night it requires fumbling with the phone, then being half-blinded by the screen when I turn it on long enough to check the time. I looked to this alarm clock to resolve this for me and in terms of timekeeping it’s exactly what I hoped. As a radio, though, it leaves much to be desired.

The main feature of this clock that makes it worth the cost is the tremendous display. The numbers are huge and are red which does not ruin night vision. And, being always on all I have to do it look at it and know the time without fumbling in the dark for my phone. The projection on the ceiling is also great and I like being able to flip it at the touch of a button. For me, this is all I need.

However, where it fails is in the audio department. The speaker is sub-par and when listening to music to does not do well at all and sounds bad though not awful. I have heard worse. I would rather see this sell for $10 more and have a better speaker in it.

If you choose this alarm clock, get it for the display which is great and is the main selling point. If you are looking for a good clock radio and the sound is important to you, this might not be the best choice. I don’t care about the audio so this is a minor point; others may feel differently.

text_fidelity_a:
Led Ring Light 18 Inch Selfie Light Circle Light kit with Tripod Stand, Dimmable 3000K- 6500K Lights for iPhone with Phone Holder, Lighting for Video Recording, Makeup, Live Stream, YouTube Equipment Note: There is more than one product attached to this listing. I am specifically reviewing the 18” light.

One of the things I have been researching for a while is ring lights. I have wanted one for a little while, but not the kind that sits on a desk and is only useful for making personal videos for upload. I wanted one that would be suitable for taking portrait photos and would be suitable for professional use. This is a nice ring light to that end and so far I am pleased with it, though I have not been using it long.

This is a large light, 18” in diameter which makes it quite a bit larger than most ring lights available right now. It is large enough that you can shoot photos or video through it using a full-sized camera with little effort, which is what I was looking for. It comes with a full-sized tripod (which it needs) as well as a nylon carry bag. It also comes with a mounting makeup mirror in the bag which is something I will not use with the ring light (I have other uses for it). In includes all of the hardware you need for mounting your camera, video camera or phone if you are a vlogger or content maker.

The very first thing I did with this light was point my camera right at it while using the electronic shutter, in order to determine if the LEDs in this light are strobing or not. I half expected these to strobe based on the price, but they do not which is a very good thing. It means steady, consistent light that does not flicker.

There are two adjustment knobs that are on the light assembly, one to control the brightness and the other to control the light temperature. The temperature range (speaking in generalized, observable terms rather than technical terms with numbers) allows for setting the light from an orangy golden-hour glow to a piercing frosty blue, and everywhere in between. So, though it may require some messing it allows for getting the light temperature just right based on skin tone and background. The brightness can be varied from a soft glow to bright enough to hurt your eyes when looking right at the ring. Thought not designed for such, this would work as a studio light in a pinch...

I do not have a light meter to check the actual light temperature or the lumens/lux output.

There’s a plastic cover over the LED array that helps to diffuse the lights and make them easier to face when using the light to illuminate a face for portraits.

The power source is AC 110/120. Some ring lights I have seen and used have USB-based power input instead. These tend to be smaller and less powerful.

Construction is good though I would stop short of saying it is solid and rugged. It is mostly plastic so it does have some flex to it but seems sturdy enough to handle getting moved around and jostled some. Because the housing is plastic instead of metal this is a lightweight unit and is easy to transport. This is a trade-off I have seen with tripods as well – lightweight for travel, heavier for less mobile work. This light seems geared for the traveler based on that.

Overall, I am pleased with this light. It is a bit better than I expected and it has everything you need in the package to be suitable for vlogging or studio use. SanDisk Ultra Fit 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive - SDCZ43-128G-GAM46 It just landed in the return envelope today... There has been three major things that led to this:
1) The Vault software stopped responding and started crashing every time I tried to run it. Data inside it were obviously inaccessible. So...
2) I decided to make it brand new and reformat the drive. Using just Windows explorer it did not work (refused), then using disk management - no success, finally using prompt and unconditional formatting (both full and quick) would end up in reporting that disk is not accessible - apparently there is writing protection on it that I could not get passed and it would not allow me to reformat it. So...
3) After attempting to reformat the disk became unreadable and Windows could not see it (disk management would see it as raw partition, not able to format it). Next, I took it off the USB port in order to reinsert it and then I almost burned my finger! This thing was so HOT I could fry an egg on it, if it was bigger! After reinserting into the USB port it would still be unrecognizable.
In short, the disk became a small brick and landed in the return envelope.
Avoid SanDisk as they apparently shovel the write protection down your throat and you can't do anything with your drive later on. So much for your customer flexibility with your product. Rather pick a very similar, ultra-small Samsung USB drive of the same size, also available from Amazon. That one comes clean (i.e. no imposed software nor writing protection) and apparently does not heat at all, or very little compared to this little oven.
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk Ultra Fit 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive - SDCZ43-128G-GAM46

text_fidelity_a:
Jabra Elite 65t Earbuds – Alexa Built-in, True Wireless Earbuds with Charging Case, Copper Black – Bluetooth Earbuds Engineered for The Best True Wireless Calls and Music Experience I agree with the other reviewer who said they look like hearing aids (before anyone jumps down my throat, nothing wrong with hearing aids, except that's not the look I'm going for, especially at this price point). I expected a much more light gold/pearl color earbud, and instead received an ugly flat ivory/gold pair and also look much larger in my ear than I had anticipated. As soon as I put them in, I thought to myself that they look like hearing aids, and when I saw the other person's Amazon review indicating the same, knew I wasn't crazy.

I tested them out for a bit and they were super easy to pair, sound quality seemed very good (compared to much less expensive wireless earbuds I have purchased on Amazon), and the button press controls seemed intuitive. However, I could tell they would become quite uncomfortable after extended periods of time. Not only are they large, but you have to press the buttons (especially on the left bud which controls volume and song skipping) pretty hard to get them to work, which presses them in to your ear even more, and that ends up hurting after a while. However, I will say that when I first put them in, they fit very snugly and I would not hesitate to use them for working out.

I am going to go with my first pick and try out the Samsung Galaxy Buds instead as they are supposed to have a sleeker profile than these. If I didn't already have the Galaxy Buds in mind, I would stick with the Jabras but go for the black color.

**EDIT 7/21/19**: I ended up buying the Samsung Galaxy Bud and enjoy them significantly more. Rather than buttons, they function by gestures (ie, tap once for play/pause, tap twice for next song/answer call, etc.), and you can customize what you want a long hold to do in the app that connects to the buds. In addition, they are smaller and have a much sleeker profile as I had expected!
text_fidelity_b: Jabra Elite 65t Earbuds – Alexa Built-in, True Wireless Earbuds with Charging Case, Copper Black – Bluetooth Earbuds Engineered for The Best True Wireless Calls and Music Experience

text_fidelity_a:
Edifier P841 Comfortable Noise Isolating Over-Ear Headphones with Microphone and Volume Controls - White This is an extremely comfortable to wear set of lightweight over-ear headphones.

There's often a lot of noise in my house. A television on somewhere, dishes being done, and a nine year old that never stops talking. I like to use headphones as an escape. When headphones claim they are noise isolating I hold them to it. These headphones did not disappoint me. The nicely cushioned soft pleather covered ear cups adjust for angle to offer a secure fit that provides excellent insulation against ambient noise and are very comfortable to wear, even for extended periods of time.

I found that they could deliver the snap of live instruments, or the impression that I was at a club with the singer on the stage in front of me. When the music had stopped, there was still silence. I noticed that I enjoyed wearing them because of the peace and quiet, I didn't want to take them off actually. These headphones isolate out noise so well they made me consider wearing them when the kid's home just to be able to hear myself think.

The sound quality is crisp, great clarity not overpowering and provide a personal ambience. They offer a great balance and at no point was I confused when watching movies. They were even picking up the weighty and seismic bass from Jurassic Park that would imply a dinosaur was right behind me. The adjustable aluminum headphone band has a slight amount of padding beneath the pleather covered top part, but I wish it had just a little bit more to provide a bit more cushioning. Finally, the headphones are able to smoothly swivel flat for storage or packing although the cable is too long for me to want to use these for trips.

Overall I am incredibly happy with their quality, especially for the price. They're very comfortable, provide excellent noise isolation, and deliver very clean response with deep bass. I plan to enjoy using them and am pleased to recommend them on Amazon.

Retail sample provided at no cost by Edifier for my testing, evaluation, and review.
text_fidelity_b: Edifier P841 Comfortable Noise Isolating Over-Ear Headphones with Microphone and Volume Controls - White

text_fidelity_a:
Inspection Camera, AsperX Endoscope Borescope, 8MM 1080P HD Snake Camera with Front-View & Side-View Dual Camera 6 LED Lights, 16.4 ft Cable, IP67 Waterproof, 32 GB Card I used to have a cheaper one where you connect it to your smartphone, so when I saw this I grabbed it. I read two reviews where one said you cannot record 1080p, but the other said that you could. You know there are cheap cameras everywhere recording 1080p. For $90, I'm disappointed to confirm the reviewer who said this only records videos in VGA and snap pictures at 720p. 1080p is only for onscreen viewing. This won't be a big deal for me since I'm not in a profession that uses this daily. I figure it's nifty to have in the toolbox, and perhaps know my way around my walls. For example, last month I drilled a hole into my wall, thinking I can drop some cables down, but the cables hit a horizontal beam. I think in construction this is called a fire stop. Hopefully this will help me learn the paths I could take in my walls.

For a professional who will use this daily, who perhaps would like to bring back a picture or a video and blow it up on his monitor for a more detailed view, 1980's VGA quality is a big thumbs down! The build quality is also not substantial either. Everything is plastic. The whole unit is about 13.5 ounces.

I do like all the provided accessories, especially the hook. I can see how that will come in handy. To view something in the wall or pipe and to pry it out with the hook. The cable is stiff and bendable allowing you to position your lens just the way you want it.

IMPORTANT ADVICE REGARDING MICRO SD CARD!!!
------------------------------------------------------------
Be very careful when removing and inserting the sd card. You have to be sure to look at the slot, and be sure you slide the card in completely horizontal. If you slide it in at an angle, it will actually still go in, completely in! I made this mistake and the card was rattling around behind the LCD screen. LOL! Luckily, the screen was easy to take apart. Just 5 screws in the back and I was able to pry it in half and retrieve my card. When inserting the card, remember the orientation... with the LCD screen facing the ceiling, the card's gold contact side should also be facing the ceiling.

This is a 5 star product for hobbyist like me. I don't see myself recording much, if at all. For a professional, I think the shortcomings make it a 3 star product. So I'm rating this a 4.
text_fidelity_b: Inspection Camera, AsperX Endoscope Borescope, 8MM 1080P HD Snake Camera with Front-View & Side-View Dual Camera 6 LED Lights, 16.4 ft Cable, IP67 Waterproof, 32 GB Card

Telescopes for Adults Astronomy - 700x90mm AZ Astronomical Professional Refractor Telescope for Kids Beginners Astronomy with Advanced Eyepieces, Cool Christmas Astronomy Gift for Men, White THE FACTS:
--------------
* Complete set to get you stargazing right away.
* Is this a refractor, reflector, or catadioptric telescope? This is a refractor telescope!
* 700mm focal length. This length is equivalent to the length of your actual refractor telescope.
* Aperture: 90mm aperture.
* Maximum magnification of this telescope is 180x. You derive at this number by multiplying the aperture (90mm) by 2.
* Eyepieces included: 25mm, 9mm. To calculate magnification of your telescope. Take 700mm divide it by the eyepiece you're using. So if you're using the 25mm eyepiece, your magnification is 28x. So you shouldn't buy eyepieces less than 4mm focal length since 700/4= 175x. So a 4mm eyepiece gets you to the max essentially.
* 3x barlow lens included. Used to increase the magnification of your telescope 3x. How do you use this? Eyepiece goes inside the barlow lens, then everything goes inside the telescope. Using a 25mm eyepiece in the example above, we get 28x magnification. So if you combine the 25mm eyepiece with the barlow, you get 84x magnification.
* 1 Finder scope and 1 finder scope bracket included: Some googling, I found this.... "A finderscope uses low power with a wide field of view and assists you in locating objects to observe through the main telescope. Crosshairs aid in centering the object you seek."
* Smartphone adapter included.
* 1 tripod tray included.

There are lots of YT tutorials. I'm just sharing with you info I've learned. From a newbie's perspective this set is very impressive, and more than enough to get going. Once you get more experienced, then I believe you can compare and contrast telescope qualities as you try out others. For now, I have no experience to compare this to anything else. Just getting my feet wet. This is 5-Stars for a beginner!

text_fidelity_a:
GAOMON PD1560 15.6 Inches 8192 Levels Pen Display with Arm Stand 1920 x 1080 HD IPS Screen Drawing Tablet with 10 Shortcut Keys TL:DR - if you want a good tablet from a brand that cares about it's customers/users AND has good drivers/software in a 16" screen you can't go wrong with this device. Huion Kamvas Pros are good and all, but I've heard too many issues compared to this device with virtually none. Especially considering the total cost is around 350 - 375.

It's not perfect and pickier users like me may not like some of the workarounds, but for a first art tablet that is basically what I'd consider the best package and/or intro into digital art you can't go wrong.

The GAOMON PD1560 really surprised me with it's performance to price ratio. The device itself is light weight and comes with what I would dub as a starter bundle of accessories. Tablet, Stand, Glove, Nibs, Carrying case, etc. The line quality is also really amazing and when running my tests didn't notice any abnormal line wobble if any at all. Brad Coblow does a good review of it. Contratry to his review the quality isn't bad at all. If you've handled a computer monitor this tablet feels like it more or less. Drivers weren't an issue and the hot keys were fantastic.

The pen kept a great charge and felt nice to use along with the included artist glove (I got only a single two finger one). Drawing without the screen protector was a little squeaky at times, but had no issue in CS6 and CSP. The tablet stays nearly completely when you adjust the brightness/backlit to sub 65 degrees F. Luckily it doesn't change the looks all that much. There is a bit of parallax and calibration can take some time to get completely right but pen accuracy is top notch.

Screen quality is good and the cables are pretty rigid so no worries there. They actually connect by recessing into a slot rather than on the edge of the device.

Lastly is customer service. I really enjoyed GAOMON's customer service which I wish more companies would do.

There are a few caveats though. To get the pen the most accurate no matter where you point on the screen you need to understand where you touch the dot when calibrating. Next you need to hold the pen in the exact same orientation and way when you draw. That means holding the pen the exact same way with little deviation of that angle to get things to line up as well as say an iPad Pro. If you don't the distance when you calibrate really well is under say... 0.5mm or less. I am really stingy about this, but for someone who isn't this isn't a big thing to worry about.

Next are the hotkeys which act more like a macbook's butterfly keyboard in terms of presses. They press well and have very little travel almost like the old iphone home buttons. This may bother some, but didn't for me. I did need to place some tape with texture to understand where my buttons were without looking.

The screen protector I didn't install and I found it really annoying to even attempt to install. Then again I've written with fountain pens for 5 years now so am very used to buttery smooth pen work.
text_fidelity_b: GAOMON PD1560 15.6 Inches 8192 Levels Pen Display with Arm Stand 1920 x 1080 HD IPS Screen Drawing Tablet with 10 Shortcut Keys

Roku N1100 HD Media Player (Old Model) We love our Roku box. We have had it about 6 months now with hardly any problems. Easy to set up with our Verizon DSL wireless internet, no problems (one other reviewer said he had problems with his Verizon).

Only problems we have had are:
1. Roku has had to reconnect to internet after big storms (not really the Roku at fault there)
2. Remote is so small and easy to use that our kids (ages 2 & 4) can use it and often loose it. We really need to invest in a good universal or an extra roku remote.

We purchased the Roku Box to use with Netflix before you could even use it with Amazon and we have not even looked at the Amazon movies yet because we never run out of things to watch. Netflix is our only source of TV/Movie selection. We do not subscribe to cable and we don't even have an antenna hooked up. I know it sounds like we are extremely primitive, but we seriously never run out of things to watch.

In reply to other reviewers that have had problems hooking up the Roku and having to turn it off to use other devices, we do have a PS2 and a Wii and surround sound set up through a switcher box and we do not have to turn the Roku Box off to get the other devices to work. We have no problem switching back and forth even with an old JVC TV.

In conclusion, we LOVE our Roku and couldn't do without it. We recommend it to all our friends and family and we are looking into getting a second box, as long as the wireless connection will work as well in the other room.

UPDATE 2011: Our Roku is now broken, will not power on. I have tried different outlets and even bought a new adapter but it will still not power on. It has never been abused. Roku Customer Service is horrible!!! basically after telling me to do all the things I had already done (and told them I had done) they told me it was broke and I needed to buy a new one. What a waste of time. Not sure if we will buy a new one or not.

Sony ICF-506 Analog Tuning Portable FM/AM Radio, Black, 2.14 lb Growing up I always had a radio in my room. Times are a little different now and I tend to get my music from the Internet, but there are still times when local radio stations are a better choice - particularly during power outages or when getting local news. I have had very good fortune with Sony electronics and computers in the past so I was eager to try this AM/FM tuner and had high expectations. It did not disappoint me.

Let me very clear about this unit - it is for AM/FM receiving only. It does not play MP3’s, it doesn’t play CDs and it doesn’t stream from the Internet. It’s just an AM/FM tuner. It does this quite well, though - better than most other tuners I have used in the last several years.

Right out of the box, this unit looks nostalgic. It has a classic AM/FM radio look and feel, very similar to a radio my father used to have in his workshop when I was a kid. This is a big plus for me, just for the fact that it takes me back to my childhood.

I plugged it in and turned it on, and I immediately tuned to one of the [relatively] local stations. It picked it up and played it very clearly, better than most other tuners I have used in the last 4-5 years. It is definitely better than the car’s radio. I “surfed” the dial and found other stations that I have listened to in the past but thought were out of range and this little radio did a good job of picking them up and playing with minimal static. That’s really all I could ask. It’s not a miracle radio though and it cannot pick up FM stations hundreds of miles away, but it has better range than most I have used recently.

I like that it can be used on AC power or on batteries. That will be handy during weather events.

I can’t find any real reason to complain about this tuner. It works great and looks great too. It is a little on the pricey side which is par for the course for Sony electronics, but it is a fine tuner that is worth its asking price.
text_fidelity_b: Sony ICF-506 Analog Tuning Portable FM/AM Radio, Black, 2.14 lb

text_fidelity_a:
ClearClick 4K HD Capture Box - Capture Up to 4K30 Video from Gaming Devices & HDMI Sources - No Computer Required I've been doing a lot of live event streaming and usually have OBS software running to also record. Having this device however means I don't need to record in the software and/or use it as a backup, as this will offload the recording directly to my SSD drive I have plugged into it!
I have an Atmos Ninja recorder I sometimes use as well, however it is picky about the source (if there's a splitter or adapter in the middle, it doesn't like it), whereas this seems to accept almost anything I throw at it so far. I like that. Also, the fact that it can bump all the way to 4K is pretty sweet too, as I can even use the original Sony A7S (which only recorded 1080 internally) as a full 4K recorder now! Cons are that it doesn't really have a display to tell you what's going on so you need to rely on the little LED colors to figure it out. Plugging a field monitor into the HDMI out helps, as you can see the output as well as the "rec" label on-screen.
NOTE: DO NOT use the output of this box as your stream or other devices in a chain, as the output is NOT a clean copy of the original! Imagine that this box is using your monitor/TV/output as its own screen, with its own overlays and all. One other reviewer mentioned that it appeared cropped on the output versus what his camera showed. All-New Fire HD 8 Screen Protector,Tempered Glass Screen Protector Film for All-New Fire HD 8 Tablet with Alexa (7th 2017 Release) [9H Hardness] [Crystal Clear] [Bubble Free] I've used glass screen protectors on several smartphones and digital cameras. This is my first time trying a large glass screen protector on a tablet. The kit contains everything you need, including a alcohol towel for cleaning your tablet (and your fingers), a sticker that tries to pick up all the lint on the tablet and the screen protector, and various other things that are less necessary. The glass is fine. It is slightly smaller than the Fire 8's screen (so you have some leeway if you don't install it perfectly). There is a little hole at the top so it doesn't cover the selfie camera. Honestly, I haven't noticed much difference between different brands of screen protectors.

If you've never installed a glass screen protector before, look on YouTube for tutorials. All of the similar products are installed the same way. You need to be really careful when installing this thing since it is large and difficult to align with your tablet's screen. I suggest that you try to align one edge of the protector as well as the camera hole and then hope for the best with the other edges. Make sure you pick up all the lint on both the tablet screen and the back of the screen protector, since any stray dust or lint is going to be noticeably ugly for as long as you have the screen protector installed. If you try to remove the screen protector to wipe off some lint that you missed, I guarantee that more lint will sucked in and make the problem worse, so you're best off doing a very thorough cleaning job the first time.

Whether or not you actually need a screen protector is a good question. If you use a case with a cover, then your chance of scratching the screen is small. I guess that depends on how rough you are with your tablet. You can go by your experience with other devices. A tablet is not like a smartphone that is sitting in your pocket with loose change and keys.
text_fidelity_b: All-New Fire HD 8 Screen Protector,Tempered Glass Screen Protector Film for All-New Fire HD 8 Tablet with Alexa (7th 2017 Release) [9H Hardness] [Crystal Clear] [Bubble Free]

ZUMIMALL Security Cameras Wireless Outdoor-2K Home Security Camera Battery Powered, Outdoor Security Cameras with 3MP Color Night Vision/Spotlight/IP66 Waterproof/PIR Detection/2-Way Talk/Cloud/SD I have been testing and reviewing WiFi cameras for the last five years. Over that time the industry has seen major advances which has led to incredible availability of high quality cameras at very reasonable costs. I have tested nearly 100 cameras and it takes a bit to impress me but I must say this set did just that.

I had no problem setting this camera up on my network. I set it both up after fully charging them in about a half hour with no issues.

Due to security precautions I never use cloud based storage in relation to WiFi cameras because that amount of constant data transfer opens your network to unnecessary hacking. The only cameras that I employ in my home allow for local storage - whether to a dedicated hard drive or individual micro SD held within each camera. This camera can hold up to a 128GB micro SD card. The card will over write the oldest data first - how much footage the card holds is dictated by the settings you select. Due to the fact these cameras only record when motion is detected a 128GB card will hold quite a lot and should suffice for 99% of people.

It’s important to know that by default the camera is set to record and save to the cloud. That can easily be reset in preference settings. In addition if you don’t install a micro SD card your camera will only capture still images when viewing - if you don’t have two extra micro SD cards order two when purchasing this set.

The camera provides a crystal clear 1080p footage and I found the motion activation very responsive. With my mesh WiFi network I encountered no lag in viewing - typically camera lag has to do with individual network properties rather than the camera itself.

The batteries in these cameras are phenomenal and actually last as long as is claimed in the listing. The battery’s life will be dictated by how often the camera is activated by motion but I have had both cameras installed and running now for over 2 months without having to recharge yet.

In my tests I found this to be an excellent budget friendly WiFi camera set that as long as you utilize the micro SD card feature is quite secure. Not having to run power cables is a major advantage and will allow these to be placed in far more places. The internal batteries are excellent and are sure to impress. The app is well designed, intuitive and easy to use even for beginners.

This is an all around excellent set of wireless WiFi cameras that I have recommended and do to you as well.

Thanks for reading my review. I enjoy writing them as I value reading other’s reviews when I’m making a buying decision. I regularly update my reviews to reflect any changes I may discover and to include helpful tips you may need if you purchase the product. text_fidelity_a:
Portable Pocket WOWOTO Projector Android Mini Smart LED DLP Projector I was actually really shocked at how great this little portable speaker is. My cell phone found it in seconds, and in less than a minute I was listening to music from my cell phone, only out of this little speaker, it actually sounded great. In fact, the bass was so effective out of this thing that some of my favorite songs made it dance around the table.

I love that it is so much louder than the music I get out of my cell phone, and I also love that I can listen to hip-hop and rap and enjoy actual bass, which usually doesn't come through for my cell phone speaker at all.

You can actually control the music from your cell phone from the speaker itself. It has a pause/play button, forward and back, and volume controls. It also has a speakerphone control, in case you wanted to have a quick conversation from the speaker itself. I would not personally want to use the speaker as a speakerphone, but it is nice to have the option in a pinch.

The one thing I didn't care for is that when you tap the volume button and it hits its maximum, it beeps at you to let you know that it won't go any louder. It's a pretty annoying sound, and in my view they could just have left that feature out. I'm sure I would figure it out soon enough that it wouldn't go any louder.

Overall, I was really surprised at the quality, ease of setup, and range of sound from this cute little speaker. I'm delighted to own it, and anticipate it getting a lot of use over the coming months and years.
text_fidelity_b: Portable Pocket WOWOTO Projector Android Mini Smart LED DLP Projector
