Logitech G502 Proteus Spectrum RGB Tunable Gaming Mouse, 12,000 DPI On-The-Fly DPI Shifting, Personalized Weight and Balance Tuning with (5) 3.6g Weights, 11 Programmable Buttons I’m not a hardcore gamer anymore, so for the past few years, I’ve been using a Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball (thumb trackball). I like trackballs for everyday use, and it’s adequate for casual World of Warcraft playing. Most of the time I just futz around leveling alts or doing 5 mans with friends.

But lately I’ve been wanting a mouse I can customize, with more options to adjust my playstyle. It’s cold in my house in the winter, so I wanted to set up mouseover macros and use more mouse buttons, because my hands are cold sitting on the keyboard. So the G502 Proteus Spectrum seemed like a good mouse to review.

I just had one problem: my computer can’t customize the mouse. Why? I have a Mac Book Air.

Now, I know the G502 says on the box that it supports Windows. There’s no mention of Mac support. But I’ve never had a problem with my Mac recognizing Logitech mice, so I figured I’d be safe. What I didn’t know is that Logitech gaming mice have separate software from the Logitech Control Center for regular Logitech mice.

After some Googling, I found the Logitech Gaming Software, which supports Mac OS X 10.8.x and up. I installed it on a Mavericks machine and a Yosemite machine. Neither computer’s Logitech Gaming Software was able to find the mouse. The G502 Proteus CORE is supported, but not the G502 Proteus SPECTRUM.

So right now, I’m unable to customize any of the extra buttons or RGB lighting or any of the other special features. It’s a really fancy basic mouse. I will continue to check for Proteus Spectrum support in the Mac Logitech Gaming Center, and update this review when I can customize things. I’m going into so much detail on the Mac side of things because I know I’m not the only Mac person who tried to use this mouse. I think there’s a workaround with Bootcamp or using a Windows computer, but I’m unable to try that.

I did use the mouse for a few weeks, to test the comfort. I’m really picky on how mice feel in my hand. I’m female and have smaller hands. I like how this mouse didn’t feel too short, and it wasn’t too heavy or wide for me to use comfortably for hours at a time. I also liked the included weights, so you can adjust the weight of the mouse. I haven’t had a mouse with an adjustable weight before, and I liked that extra level of customization.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech G502 Proteus Spectrum RGB Tunable Gaming Mouse, 12,000 DPI On-The-Fly DPI Shifting, Personalized Weight and Balance Tuning with (5) 3.6g Weights, 11 Programmable Buttons

text_fidelity_a:
Magellan Triton 400 Waterproof Hiking GPS UPDATE 11-30-2009: I initially gave this unit a rating of 3 stars. I am upgrading it to 4 stars because of a firmware upgrade that vastly improved the speed of the unit and eliminated issues I saw with VantagePoint. That said, I am leaving my original write-up intact.

---

I am an avid geocacher, and I have other hand-held units by Garmin and DeLorme. I have never used a Magellan GPS though I have friends who have used an Explorist for years with reasonable results. I was anxious to try out this unit to see if Magellan puts out a good product. In a nutshell, it is a mixed bag though overall the Triton 400 is a nice unit.

This is a very small unit, a little smaller than my Garmin eTrex Legend which is a fairly simple unit. Small is not necessarily a bad thing. It fits nicely in a pocket or a stash bag, being about the size of a cell phone.

The display is small too and people who want a large display will not like this unit. That said, the display is very bright, crisp and clear, everything being quite visible and readable. It had, in my opinion, the best general display of the units I have used, surpassing even the DeLorme in display quality.

Once the unit is powered on, it quickly starts finding satellites. Though it switches to navigation mode quickly, it is important to remember that the unit may or may not have a good lock on satellites - it may still be acquiring more. Be cautious in this regard, until used to using this unit.

The Triton has small buttons. I have big fingers. Surprisingly, this does not seem to be an issue, as I have not yet had the misfortune of mis-keying anything.

Several reviewers have complained that the menu system on the Triton is confusing, unintuitive and hard to use. I did not find this to be the case. I can simply say they are different than Garmin's implementations. That is neither good nor bad - just, different. Once used to them, this unit is no less intuitive than any other unit.

Navigation is straightforward and easy. When navigating I have found the unit to be on par with my Garmin GPSMap 60CSx, which is usually fairly accurate. I've no complaints in this regard.

My disappointment with the Triton mostly involve what's [not] in the box and the software that the computer uses to interact with it. There is a single CD in the box that includes PDF versions of the manual. There are no printed manuals in the box, at all. This is ok, but other units include a manual so it would be nice if this one did too. There is also a link to the website where you can download Vantage Point, the software for working with the unit. The software is 42MB, and I am on dial-up. Even including an older version would have been nice since there is plenty of room on the CD for it...

When the software is loaded on a Windows Vista machine, system behavior becomes very sluggish, mouse movement being choppy and COM port communications getting interruptions - enough interruptions to disconnect from the Internet. Though the software has eye appeal and offers a lot of functionality for dealing with the GPS, it drips of slowness. When sending caches to the unit, it sends at a rate of about 1 every 5-10 seconds, which means sending 500 at a time would take a good deal of time. That said, geocache information stops a little shy of being a paperless solution - the unit retains description, terrain/difficulty, owner and hint information, but it does not offer previous logs, sizes or other important bits of information. It's a good reference in the field but not sufficient to go true paperless.

Though there is a place on the bottom of the unit for a lanyard, it is disappointing that there is none in the box.

One area of real concern for me is the connection interface for the unit. The connector on the unit is exposed and uncovered, with nothing to keep it from getting dirty. If nothing else there should be a rubber flap over it, or a cover, or *something*.

This is actually a nice unit, with a decent feature set and good accuracy. Magellan cut some corners and left out some details that keep this from being a great unit. The technology is there. The design is there. The details are not. Hopefully Magellan will close the gap on these details soon.
text_fidelity_b: Magellan Triton 400 Waterproof Hiking GPS

But the volume control and power control on the remote is a very good plus over the basic remote. The battery compartment for remote is a little tricky to get opened at first but if you just apply a slight pressure at the same time as sliding the compartment down jt will slide right open. And getting to the streaming quality it will depend on which app you are using. Surprising to me is that the Amazon Prime Video app uses a lot more wifi data than most of the other apps making the shows and movies buffer quite a bit sometimes. I am curious why Amazon Prime uses so much more data vs Netflix or Hulu for example but it surely does. And if you have a Roku device and are used to the Rokus functions it will take a bit of getting used to how the Firestick apps are downloaded and stored compared to the Roku. But they both have equally good and bad comparisons when it comes to their individual functions. Both have excellent picture and sound. What i would really like is for Amazon's firestick to have a remote control app for your android or ios phone. Roku does have the free remote app to download and works great navigating and also has alexa voice control and tou can plug earphones into your phone for private listening. And also remember when buying a firestick to check the gift box if it is going to be used by someone else in their home. If you check the connect to my account box instead all of your information on your other firesticks will be on the new one and also the Amazon buying app with your personal information. text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro 12.2 (32GB, Black) This is a flawless tablet. Everything you'd expect. There are a few things that don't feel comfortable or might feel jarring, but then you are here because you want a huge tablet, so they should be expected.

The screen if gorgeous! And Samsung has done a great job of making the icons proportional to the screen. Because at this super high resolution, if you left the icons to the normal size, they would be TINY. That said, be prepared to see -huge- icons since they are proportionally bigger than, say, even a huge Note 3 phone. Still the ratio isn't one to one from a tiny tablet, there is room for a couple of more icons per row.

Weight: This is light and feels great... for a tablet its size. That said, be prepared to always have to put it or your hands on something if you are using it more than a couple of minutes. While it is solid & light enough to hold it in one hand by a corner and use, your hand will be cramping in no time.

Look and feel: Just awesome. I don't get professional reviewers issue with "faux leather", it looks and feels awesome! Even though it's bigger than all the rest, this is still a tablet, as I said above, you can brag and pick it up by a corner without feeling like you are putting too much force on a corner or anything of the nature. But its dimensions do mean you have to lean your arm on something or put it down for using more than reading a single email, even then...

The large dimensions also mean awkward reading in bed unless you are sitting up with your legs or a pillow under it. If you are laying on the ground or on your bed faxing down with it flat and reading websites or an online book with the tablet in portrait format (as one would tend to read long things), then the top is too far away and an angle, as would a tall magazine be.

This can easily be fixed with a little something to prop the end away from you up of course, but just making sure you realize that you will get what you are asking for, a gorgeous, great feeling tablet that is the largest on the market, but you are also getting something rather large, and all that comes with that, so expect it. I read all professional reviews saying pretty much that and I figured they were just complaining to have something to write about... nope, it really is a bit hard to wield.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro 12.2 (32GB, Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm Instax Wide 300 Instant Film Camera (Black) Boy! does this camera remind me of my old Polaroid Square Shooter. This camera is NOTHING like your iPhone camera as it's big, and totally analog except for the film counter on the back. I love it when the motor runs and film comes sliding out - a sound I well remember. I think the hardest thing about using this camera was getting the shoulder strap put on, other than that it's very easy to use. Though it is on the big side, it doesn't weigh much and the view finder and shutter button are pretty much intuitive. I'm left handed so holding it like a right-hander took a little getting used too, but it's not a problem for me. This camera is made for right-handers so those who are very much left-handed might not like the way you have to hold it, and the shutter button is on the right side front. It has flash and you can adjust the light/dark and distance to you subject with minimal effort.

Loading the film was easy, aiming at my subject was easy, the shutter button was easy to depress and everything is/was easy. The close-up adapter looks like there's no way it will attach itself to the lens, but somehow it does. I took one close-up of my dog but the picture didn't turn out very good because she moved away right when I hit the shutter button-but that's typical for her. I haven't taken a "selfie" yet but it seems like it will be easy to do.

The color development of the film is pretty good. I took a wide angle picture of my raised garden beds and I was able to get all of them in the picture and the various green colors were vivid. I also took a picture of the front of our house, and though I had to still walk across the street to our neighbor's driveway to get the entire house in the view finder, the picture turned out nice. Again, the colors were bright and vivid. It got the entire house plus some area on both sides. In the past with my other cameras I would have to get further away or be happy with just most of the house in the picture so it's real nice to get the whole thing with room to spare.

The film is kind of pricey. For a pack of 40 pictures it costs around $34.00. I figured it would be kind of expensive and I hope the price of the film goes down some. This is a comfort camera for those of us who grew up with Polaroids. It may be that since we are living in highly uncertain and stressful times, having a camera like this is a cool blast from the past and may make us just feel better having one like this, plus it takes nice pictures.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm Instax Wide 300 Instant Film Camera (Black)

text_fidelity_a: Beats Studio Wireless Over-Ear Headphone - Matte Black (Old Model) These headphones do have a more balanced sound than the horrible original Beats that were just too bass heavy. The Bluetooth pairing was quick and easy and battery life is decent. The case and accessories seem to be good quality. In all honesty though for the sound quality I'd never pay the retail asking price for these or recommend them to anyone. I got a used pair (yes they are real Beats) for half the price of new and at this price point I feel it's worth it. The noise canceling isn't anything to write home about and if it's a big reason why you're considering these I'd look to Bose or elsewhere where it's done much better. Another point with these is comfort. They're ok for an hour or so, but I'd not want these on pushing two or more. They tend to pinch at the ear cup level and you can see in various pics how the cups nearly touch when not on the head. So the farther you are pushing those cups out the more they are fighting to close so to speak. I don't have a large head, I don't expand the headband at all when wearing, and they get a little clampy after a bit. Another comfort issue is the interior depth of the ear cups. I don't have big ear or ones that stick out and I still feel my ears slightly pushing against the speaker. I couldn't imagine anyone with large ears being happy with these at all and if you fall into that category I'd definitely try on a pair in a store before buying. The cup pads are nice and it's too bad they didn't make them just a tad deeper.  So in summary these are good headphones if not great ones, but honestly not worth retail. The Bluetooth is nice, but you're obviously paying for image here.
text_fidelity_b: Beats Studio Wireless Over-Ear Headphone - Matte Black (Old Model)

text_fidelity_a:
Toshiba TY-CWU700 Vintage Style Retro Look Micro Component Wireless Bluetooth Audio Streaming & CD Player Wood Speaker System + Remote, USB Port for MP3 Playback, FM Stereo Digital Tuner, AUX Input This unit is large and not at all like the dimensions listed on Amazon. It is 5 inches high (top to bottom), 8 inches deep (front to back), and 16 inches in long (side-to-side).

WHAT COMES IN THE BOX:
- one speaker unit with both left and right speakers inside the large housing
- one power cord
- one FM antenna cord / wire
- one AAA battery
- one remote
- three user guides; one in English, Spanish, and French (I love this because I can keep the instructions in English and throw out the others)
- one limited 1-year warranty insert

FEATURES:
- Bluetooth speaker
- CD player
- FM Radio with ability for 30 preset radio stations
- Ability to operate controls via remote or front of the unit buttons
- Clock
- Sleep / timer function up to 120 minutes in 15-minute increments
- LED Dimmer
- USB terminal that supports USB memory (thumb drive) in FAT 16 or FAT 32 format
- Line In port to plug in an external audio device such as earphones / headphones

The sound this produces when I play my CDs was awesome and music to my ears. I also paired this speaker with my Google Nexus 7 Tablet (2013 version Android device) and my iPad Pro 12.9 and experienced moderately powerful sound there as well. The FM radio was staticky but that was due to the location of where I placed my unit. When I did receive a station, the sound was great.

In summary, this produces beautiful sound. As a Bluetooth speaker, it does not produce as powerful a sound as my [[ASIN:B00SNBCBBY ION Block Rocker]] but it is still good. The addition of the FM radio is a nice touch. I also like that it functions as an LED clock. The instructions and operation of the unit take a bit of getting use to and can be confusing but I was eventually able to figure it out; although I may have to consult the pamphlet every now and then. Overall, this is a well-rounded unit for indoor use but the unit is larger than I expected. It is as large as those old AM/FM amplifiers from years ago and has a retro 70’s look (see attached picture).

PS For those who are interested in comparisons, this is my sixth Bluetooth speaker. I ordered five other Bluetooth speakers over a several year period. I have a [[ASIN:B007ZG03DG Bose Wave Bluetooth Music Adapter]], which is not very good and a [[ASIN:B00MPMK3GW Goal Zero 94014 Rock Out 2 Green Solar Rechargeable Speaker]] which does not work when paired with some devices and, when it does pair well, it usually lacks the powerful sound I am looking for.

I also purchased one [[ASIN:B00SNBCBBY ION Audio Block Rocker (iPA76A) | Portable Bluetooth Speaker]] and one [[ASIN:B01N17AQ7U ION Audio IPA88 Tailgater Flash Wireless/Bluetooth Speaker]] both from Costco. I absolutely love the Block Rocker (except for when paired with my iPad Pro) and I only like the Tailgate Flash. The lights on the Tailgate Flash annoy me because they have to be turned off every time I power on the unit. Nevertheless, the sound from the ION speakers are usually awesome. The IONs are the only ones I use frequently indoors (even though they are more of an outdoor Bluetooth speaker). They are battery powered powerful speakers and the sound is intense. If one wants Bluetooth only with the capability of travelling with them without having to find a power outlet, then these are worth considering.

I also have a [[ASIN:B01MUG5WIN Sony XB20 Portable Wireless Speaker with Bluetooth, Blue (2017 model)]] which pairs well with my HP Omen Laptop and moderately well with my Nexus 7 and iPad Pro. However, this has to be charged first just like the Goal Zero speaker that I dislike.

PS My boyfriend connected his iPad 3 to this one's Bluetooth and loves it for listening to Podcasts. In order to get the volume as loud as he wanted, he also used the volume controls on the side of his iPad in conjunction with the volume knob on the Toshiba. On another note, he mentioned that the controls located below the CD player are very small for someone who has eye problems and I would agree with that. What I find inconvenient is that the button to open and close the CD player is there so that when the CD is open, I have to put my hand underneath it to close if I am not using the remote. Nevertheless, he loves this Toshiba just like I do.
text_fidelity_b: Toshiba TY-CWU700 Vintage Style Retro Look Micro Component Wireless Bluetooth Audio Streaming & CD Player Wood Speaker System + Remote, USB Port for MP3 Playback, FM Stereo Digital Tuner, AUX Input

text_fidelity_a:
SHANLONYI Radio with AM/FM, Time Projector,USB Charging for Mobile Phone, Large 7" LED Display, Dual, Battery Backup Projection Alarm Clock, Black-red ¡­ I'm wavering a bit on how I should rate the SHANLONYI Radio with AM/FM, Time Projector. On the one hand, I like the face of the clock digits and the projection light is pretty nifty. On the other hand, I still can't figure out how to set the radio functions to save stations. But then again, setting the alarm was easy. Yet on the other hand, I keep having to re-tune the radio although I'm admittedly not used to a radio outside of the car so the issue may be more with me than the product.

Honestly, I think I'm going with the 4-star because the main reason that I wanted to try the clock was for it to be used as a clock, not a radio. I really do like the size of the digits on the clock. It makes it easy to read. It was also easy to set the time and alarm. I also like adjusting the volume of the alarm so it wakes me up but it isn't an obnoxious level of sound.

The USB port is also a nice-to-have. The radio does get decent reception too. It picks up the local college radio station and that can sometimes be problematic. So all in all, I rather like the clock and even the radio since I really just listen to two stations anyway.
text_fidelity_b: SHANLONYI Radio with AM/FM, Time Projector,USB Charging for Mobile Phone, Large 7" LED Display, Dual, Battery Backup Projection Alarm Clock, Black-red ¡­

text_fidelity_a:
RIVA TURBO X RTX01B Premium Wireless Bluetooth Speaker (Black) My first Bluetooth speaker was the Bose Soundlink; I then transitioned to a smaller, more portable Braven LUX. As an audiophile, when I was offered the opportunity to test drive the RIVA Turbo X, I jumped at it. The first thing I noticed right off the bat is the WEIGHT; the speaker clocks in at nearly 6 pounds (compared to the lightweight Braven, or the slightly heftier Soundlink). It's also designed like a sportscar, with a glossy black finish with red rubber accents covering access ports. The top contains streamlined buttons for Power, Surround, Bluetooth pairing, mute, up and down volume, and Turbo mode. There's also an iOS app that allows you to control the surround and turbo settings directly from your phone.

I appreciated the quick start guide handily attached to the top of the speaker; it recommends that you play the speaker at 50% volume for several hours to break them in. It comes out of the box partially charged (around 40%) meaning you can start using it immediately (which I did using David Garret's new "Explosive" album). The sound balance is fantastic; as I live in an apartment, unfortunately I'm not able to really take advantage of the Turbo mode (which boosts to over 100dB). Pairing was a snap and I was off and running. As soon as I synched with my iPad, I was prompted to download the "Ground Control" app (which as previously mentioned, gives you battery life stats, volume, and the ability to turn on surround and Turbo modes).

It also comes loaded with extras in the form of RCA cables, male-to-male audio cables, and it's also capable of charging other devices. The battery is recharged via AC (the life is around 26 hours); no USB option here. The touch buttons on top illuminate when you hold your hand over it, which is a fantastic feature in a dark room or if you're using this outside.

The sound is fantastic with just about every genre I threw at it, from Baroque opera vocals to instrumentals to EDM.

This is a serious investment that not only looks fantastic, but sounds absolutely fantastic...and my Bose Soundlink is going in the closet. If you're looking for maximum power with no trade in sound quality (especially at higher volume levels), the Riva TurboX is the way to go.
text_fidelity_b: RIVA TURBO X RTX01B Premium Wireless Bluetooth Speaker (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
B-Land 10" Ring Light with Tripod Stand & 3 Phone Holders & Flexible Clip Microphone Holder for Multicam Live Stream, LED YouTube Lighting Kit Photo Light for Videos & Photography I am best described as a skilled amateur when it comes to photography and I am always looking for ways to get better and to build my knowledge and ability. I am not a professional by any means, but I know a lot more than the average selfie-taker. I have wanted a ring light for a little while and I was delighted to have the chance to get to use this one. It does work, in the right circumstances, but it is definitely aimed at the base consumer market and is priced accordingly.

Thought it can be used as part of a professional set-up, it is designed and marketed as a consumer-grade unit. There are a number of obvious design decisions that make this more than just a little apparent. The tripod is good, but the mounts are designed for smartphones and will not work for DSLR cameras, mirrorless cameras or video cameras. That’s ok, as it is clearly marketed that way. The unit uses a USB power source which is an important point – the light itself isn’t especially bright like one that uses a normal AC power source. To be effective, the light needs to be fairly close to the subject. If a dim directional light is needed, a regular desk lamp is more than adequate in most cases. The upshot is that using USB power makes it much more portable for travel (more on that in a moment).

The remote allows for making a few adjustments to the light itself. There are three color modes and ten brightness modes, all of which can be (rather, must be) set through the remote. The adjustments are sufficient for this grade of light, though I would have found more colors and a more smooth graduation in brightness to be more useful. That’s more of a nitpick than a criticism considering the price point.

Build-wise, this unit is acceptable. It should hold up well enough in the studio or home office. What is lacking is a carry case to protect it when travelling. Considering the target audience (social media producers), this is an oversight that I think is important. To transport this light, it should be well secured and the only recourse as sold is to put it back in the original box, and that’s just unwieldy. Plan accordingly if you choose to transport this light.

This is an adequate unit for its target audience but will leave the aspiring professional underwhelmed. If you are looking for something that will work sufficiently for making posts to social media this is a reasonable unit; if you need a serious ring light for photography, consider other options. The main problem with this light is the fact that it is designed for portability but comes with no carrying case; keep this in mind.
text_fidelity_b: B-Land 10" Ring Light with Tripod Stand & 3 Phone Holders & Flexible Clip Microphone Holder for Multicam Live Stream, LED YouTube Lighting Kit Photo Light for Videos & Photography
